rationale.conceptual: The underlying method is well-established DFT calculations (PBE geometry optimization, elastic constants via stress-strain, phonons, DOS). The hardness model is a previously published semi-empirical formula, not a novel derivation. A practitioner familiar with DFT can implement the steps with standard knowledge, though the hardness model requires looking up the reference equations. No new theory or algorithmic innovation is needed.
rationale.execution: The pipeline spans 8 explicit steps: structure generation, two reference energy calculations, geometry optimization, elastic constants (multiple strained calculations), phonon dispersion, DOS, Mulliken population analysis, and hardness estimation. This requires multiple DFT runs (scf, relax, ph.x, dos.x, projwfc.x), post-processing of elastic constants, and coordination of dependencies. It is a moderately long, multi-stage workflow with several load-bearing handoffs, but all within a single DFT code suite.

difficulty.reasoning: The task reproduces a standard DFT study of zinc-blende IrC using PBE functional and Quantum ESPRESSO. The method is routine for computational materials science: geometry optimization, elastic constants, phonons, DOS, and a published semi-empirical hardness model. The pipeline is multi-step (8 steps) with dependencies between relaxation, property calculations, and post-processing, which requires careful orchestration but not extreme complexity.

compute_estimate.reasoning: The zinc-blende IrC unit cell contains only 2 atoms; the plane-wave cutoff is 350 eV. All DFT calculations (relaxation, phonons on a small supercell, DOS, etc.) are trivially small, run in minutes on a single CPU core, and require negligible memory and no external data beyond pseudopotentials.
